title: Pitch Skill
purpose: Understand how pitch is measured, how to read pitch curves, and how to convert between representations (MIDI, note name, frequency).

representations.midi: Integer 0-127. MIDI 60 = Middle C (C4). Each +1 = one semitone up.
representations.note_name: Pitch class + octave, e.g. C4, F#3, A#5. Octave 4 = middle octave.
representations.frequency_hz: MIDI to Hz: f = 440 * 2^((midi-69)/12). Hz to MIDI: midi = 69 + 12*log2(f/440).
representations.cents: 100 cents = 1 semitone. Used to describe small deviations and glides.

midi_to_octave_rule.formula: midi // 12 - 1 gives the octave; midi % 12 gives the pitch class (C=0, C#=1, ... B=11).

pitch_curve_reading.definition: A pitch tracker (e.g. CREPE, pYIN) returns the fundamental frequency (f0) over time. Convert each frame to MIDI to see the melody line.
pitch_curve_reading.stable_note: A horizontal stretch of the f0 curve at one pitch = one held note.
pitch_curve_reading.glide_meend: A continuous diagonal slope between two stable pitches = a meend/portamento (slide).
pitch_curve_reading.vibrato_gamak: A rapid periodic wobble around a stable pitch = vibrato or gamak (oscillation).
pitch_curve_reading.octave_error: If the curve jumps exactly +/-12 semitones and returns, that is an octave error — collapse to the correct register.

octave_stability.rule: The human vocal line stays within about an octave-and-a-half. It does not bounce between octaves every other note.
octave_stability.action: If adjacent notes alternate across an octave, correct to the surrounding register.
